decisionsTitle: Checkpoints and cut-off times on the route: the editor, the event page and the bib's profile
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-13:** «other things for the route: I need to put checkpoints and limit times»; on the race number: «nu pot să văd unde e punctul de alimentare pe acel număr»; and on the event's duration box («Ore / Minute», «Cât durează — de exemplu 1 oră și 45 de minute…»): «Aici nu e clar „cât durează” ce? trebuie să pot pune timp limită». Amends §718 (the route) and §750 (the bib's profile strip), §71/§433 (the duration box), §542 (the Organizer writes an event's checkpoints: the one exception to the Administrator's event row) and §751 (the event's file is version 2).

**Decision — the data.** A table of its own, `event_checkpoints` (migration `0147`, expand only): the event (deleted with it), a position, a name in Romanian and in English (both required, 60 characters each), the kilometre (`numeric(6,2)`, never negative, never beyond the route's length — the distance the club typed, else the GPX's), what is there as a closed set (`event_checkpoint_kind[]`: «Apă», «Mâncare», «Prim ajutor», «Cronometrare»; a fifth is a migration, like every state here), an optional cut-off and an optional note in both languages or neither (120 characters each). The list is read by kilometre; the position only keeps two points at the same kilometre in the order they were typed.

**The cut-off is a time of the day on the event's own clock** (`time`, in `events.timezone`), not a `timestamptz`. An instant is the right answer on the day it is typed and the wrong one the day the club moves the race: the start, the programme and the end follow the new date while a stored instant stays on the old one, and every cut-off would have to be shifted by hand. A time of the day follows the date by construction. It is counted from the race's gun when it has one, else the event's start; a cut-off at or before that start is refused, one after a farther point's cut-off is refused (a runner passes kilometre 10 before kilometre 20), and one after the end is refused. A race that ends on the next day reads a cut-off earlier than the gun's time as the next day's; any other event refuses it. The end is read on the same clock (the span from the start's minute of the day to the end's), so on the night the clocks change a cut-off after the finish closes is still refused. A refusal says the start or the time the finish closes it compares against, names the point in the backoffice's language (a row with no name by its kilometre) and writes the kilometre the language's way («21,1», «21.1»).

**The editor.** «Puncte de control» is a card of its own at the top of the editor's main column, beside the save form; the page's list of sections has it inside «Traseul» (no number, no chip of its own; «Traseul» reads as drawn while the table is), and «Traseul» says where the points are written and links to the card. Moving it visually inside «Traseul» is left to the editor's layout work. The card: add (three spare rows), change, remove («Scoate»), always shown by kilometre; the house's form primitives, 44-pixel targets, a glyph before every button's words, plain forms that work with scripts off. **The card's forms are its own, beside the editor's save form and not in it**: HTML forms cannot nest, and a refusal here — a kilometre beyond the route, said with the route's length; a cut-off before the start or after a farther point's — must keep what was typed here and nothing of the event's other boxes (the shape of §749's card). A save never deletes a point it was not told about (a colleague's point added meanwhile survives), and never brings back one a colleague removed: a posted row whose point is no longer the event's is dropped. The Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator write — **an exception to §542**, which gives every save of an event to the Administrator: where the water is and by when the last runner passes is the preparation on the ground §542 left with the Organizer, not the event's settings it took away (`roles.ts#canEditEventFields` names the exception); the list reaches the public page and the bib, so every change is audited; every other role that opens the editor reads the list as words; the role is asserted on the server and every change writes one audit row `event_checkpoints.changed` (the list before and after: kilometre, name, cut-off — the club's own work, never a participant). «Ia punctele din GPX» appears when the uploaded GPX has `<wpt>` waypoints: each is projected on the nearest stretch of the track to give its kilometre along it, its kinds guessed from its name, symbol and type; a waypoint farther than 300 m from the track is left out and counted; one past the route's end by up to 300 m (a watch's «Sosire» at 21,13 km against a typed 21 097 m) is placed at the end, one farther past it is left out and counted with the route's length. The preview lists them ticked, each with a name box per language — the file's one name in the Romanian box, the English one the club's to write, never copied (a page never shows one language's words on the other's) — and «Adaugă punctele alese» adds the ticked ones, never twice, refusing a ticked one with an empty name. **Nothing is fetched under the event's lock** (§403): the GPX is read before the transaction, and a file or typed distance that changed meanwhile is a CONFLICT.

**The rules hold after every save, not only the card's.** The event save, the series' other dates it reaches and an import over an event (unless the file's own list replaces the saved one) hold the saved checkpoints to the same rules against the event as written — a moved start or gun, a shorter «Timp limită», a shorter route or another GPX — inside the save's transaction, the GPX's length read before it opens; a save that would break one is refused, «Salvarea ar strica „Puncte de control”: …» with the rule's own sentence (and the date, on another date of a series), and nothing is written. So the page and the bib never show a cut-off before the start or after the finish, nor a point past the route, and a later save of the card is never refused over a row nobody touched. «Duplică» and a series' new dates copy the checkpoints with the route: the cut-offs are times of the day, so they follow the new date.

**«Timp limită».** The duration box keeps its column and its two boxes; its words follow the type select, with a stopwatch before them: a race asks «Timp limită» («Cât au alergătorii de la start până se închide sosirea — de exemplu 2 ore și 30 de minute. Lasă gol dacă nu există.»), every other event «Cât durează evenimentul» («De la start până la final — de exemplu 1 oră și 45 de minute. Sfârșitul se calculează singur. Lasă gol dacă nu s-a anunțat.»). **For a race the minutes count from the gun when it has one** (`duration.ts#durationBase`), so the stored end is the moment the finish closes; the editor, its summary, the night line and the event's file read the box back from the same instant, so a save that changes nothing keeps the end. A race saved before this whose gun is after its meeting time keeps its end; its box now reads the minutes from the gun. Every other event keeps its end exactly as before. **The transition:** every race already saved — the live 21 November race included — publishes «Timp limită» (and, with checkpoints, «Sosire · se închide la …») from its saved end the moment this ships, with no save; that end was typed under the old «Durata — cât durează», counted from the meeting time. The club confirms each upcoming race's «Timp limită» in «Când și unde» before the release reaches production (CLAUDE.md «Still owed» 21), and the release message names the live race.

**The event page.** «Timp limită: 2 h 30 min» under «Când» on a race. Under the route's maps, the table «Puncte de control» / «Checkpoints»: the kilometre, the point (its note under it), what is there — a chip with the glyph **and** the word, never the glyph alone — and «Ora limită 11:30»; the last row is the finish, «Sosire · se închide la 12:30», on a race with a time limit only (another event's end is when it ends, no limit). Nothing is drawn without checkpoints. At 320 pixels each row is a block, each cell with its column's word. The card's saves expire the public cache's `events` tag, as the editor's do.

**The bib's profile strip.** «Punctele de control pe profil» (on by default; drawn only with the profile and the event's checkpoints): at each kilometre an aid station is a small drawn glyph — a cup where there is water, a fork where there is food alone — above the line, or under it where the line runs too high, never out of the profile's own row, so never over the number or the name; any other point is a dot; each has a thin tick to the chart's foot and «km 12» under it where there is room. «…cu orele limită» (off by default: a time printed on paper cannot be corrected) prints «km 12 · 11:30». **The crowding rule**: a mark closer than 6 points to the one before gives way, to an aid station first; the times are printed only when every label then fits — all or none, since a number that says some cut-offs is read as the others having none; without them each «km» is printed where it clears its neighbour and the words «Start» and «Sosire»; the marks always stay. One geometry decides it for the PDF and the picture; the pictures' addresses — the bibs page's, the designer's preview (`v=`) and the desk's SQL stamp — cover the checkpoints' kilometres, kinds and cut-offs and the two ticks, so no stale picture is served. The bib's header is not touched.

**The event's JSON file (§751) is version 2**: a race's `durationMinutes` counts from the gun. A version 1 file — production's, before this release — is still read: a race with a gun and a start hour has its minutes recounted from the gun, so it imports with the end it had, and one whose old end was at or before its gun is refused rather than given a time limit nobody chose. The file carries `route.checkpoints` (kilometre, both names, kinds, cut-off, note; no id) and the two ticks. Export reads them; an import as new writes them after the event exists; an import over writes the file's list where the diff shows it changed (the diff names it «Punctele de control»). Both hold the list to the card's rules against the file's event before anything is copied or written, so a list the card would refuse refuses the whole file. A file made before checkpoints existed reads with none.

**Not changed:** registrations, the capacity, the emails, the legal texts. **Not decided here:** whether the terms should say that a runner may be stopped or timed out at a published cut-off is the lawyer's question (CLAUDE.md «Still owed» 16); any such sentence goes through the template and its approval.

**Refused:** a `timestamptz` cut-off (it drifts when the date moves, above); free-text kinds (a word the page and the bib cannot draw a glyph for); the card's boxes inside the editor's save form (a refusal there would lose the event's other boxes, and forms cannot nest); some cut-offs on a crowded bib and not others; counting a race's limit from the meeting time (the help says «de la start», and a runner's start is the gun).
changelogLine: - **Checkpoints and the race's «Timp limită»** — «Puncte de control», a card of its own beside the editor's save form, linked from «Traseul» (water, food, first aid, timing, a cut-off; from the GPX's waypoints in one press, a name in each language), a table on the event page with the finish closing time, «Timp limită: 2 h 30 min» for a race, counted from the gun, and the aid stations marked on the bib's profile strip with «km 12» and, ticked, the cut-offs. An event save that would break a saved checkpoint is refused; the event's file is version 2 and a version 1 file keeps its race's end. Every race already saved shows «Timp limită» from its saved end: confirm each upcoming race's box. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given an event with checkpoints, when its page renders, then under the route's maps the table «Puncte de control» / «Checkpoints» lists them by kilometre with the point's name and note in the page's language, what is there as chips each with its glyph and its word, and «Ora limită 11:30» or a dash read as «fără oră limită»; a race with a time limit ends the table with «Sosire» «se închide la 12:30» at the event's end on its own clock, any other event has no finish row, an event without checkpoints has no section, and at 320 pixels each row is a block whose cells carry their column's word (2026-10-13, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a race with a time limit, when its page renders, then «Timp limită» / «Time limit» says the minutes from the gun (else the start) to the end as «2 h 30 min» under «Când», with a stopwatch; no other type has the row (2026-10-13, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the event editor, when an Organizer, an Administrator or a Superadministrator saves «Puncte de control», then a name in both languages, a kilometre from 0 within the route's length (the typed distance, else the GPX's), kinds from «Apă», «Mâncare», «Prim ajutor», «Cronometrare», a cut-off as a time of the day after the start (the gun's on a race), not after the end and not after a farther point's, and a note in both languages or neither are kept, by kilometre; anything else is refused naming the box with the reason (a kilometre beyond the route says the route's length) and keeps what was typed; a point not on the form is never deleted; every change is audited as `event_checkpoints.changed`; any other role reads the list and its save is refused FORBIDDEN on the server (2026-10-13, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event whose uploaded GPX has `<wpt>` waypoints, when «Ia punctele din GPX» is pressed, then a preview lists each waypoint within 300 m of the track with its kilometre along the track (the waypoint projected on the nearest stretch) and kinds guessed from its words, ticked, and says how many were farther; «Adaugă punctele alese» adds the ticked ones through the same rules, never one already listed at the same kilometre with the same name, and a GPX replaced since the preview is a CONFLICT (2026-10-13, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The duration box is labelled by the type select with a glyph — «Timp limită» with «Cât au alergătorii de la start până se închide sosirea — de exemplu 2 ore și 30 de minute. Lasă gol dacă nu există.» on a race, «Cât durează evenimentul» with «De la start până la final — de exemplu 1 oră și 45 de minute. Sfârșitul se calculează singur. Lasă gol dacă nu s-a anunțat.» otherwise, in both languages — and a race's minutes count from its gun when it has one: the stored end is the gun plus the minutes, the editor, its summary and the event's file read the box back from the gun, and every other event's end is the start plus the minutes as before (2026-10-13, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

An event's JSON file carries `route.checkpoints` (kilometre, both names, kinds, cut-off, note; no id) and the bib's two checkpoint ticks; an import as new writes the list, an import over writes it where the diff shows «Punctele de control» changed, a list the editor's card would refuse refuses the whole import before anything is written, an export–import–export round trip gives the same list, and a file without the key reads and imports with none (2026-10-13, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Profilul traseului» and «Punctele de control pe profil» ticked (the second on by default) and an event with checkpoints, every number — sheet, picture and preview — marks each checkpoint within the printed distance on the profile strip: a drawn cup where there is water, a fork where there is food alone, a dot otherwise, a tick to the chart's foot, «km 12» under it where it clears its neighbours and «Start»/«Sosire»; with «…cu orele limită» (off by default) «km 12 · 11:30» only when every label then fits, else no time at all; a mark within 6 points of the one before gives way, to an aid station first; nothing is drawn outside the profile's row; the bibs page's, the preview's and the desk's picture addresses change when a checkpoint's kilometre, kinds or cut-off or either tick changes (2026-10-13, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event with saved checkpoints, when an event save, a series save reaching other dates, or an import over the event that does not replace the list would move the start or the gun past a saved cut-off, end the event («Timp limită») before one, or shorten the route (the typed distance, else the GPX's) under a saved point, then the save is refused naming «Puncte de control» with the rule's own sentence (and the date, on another date of a series) and nothing is written; a save that keeps every point true goes through and leaves the list as it was; «Duplică» and a series' new dates copy the checkpoints (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Ia punctele din GPX», the preview gives every waypoint a name box per language, the file's name in the Romanian one and the English one empty, and an add with an empty name is refused naming that box; a waypoint past the route's end by at most 300 m is offered at the end, one farther past it is left out and counted with the route's length; the GPX is read before the event row is locked, and a GPX or typed distance changed meanwhile is a CONFLICT; a saved row posted by a stale form whose point was removed is dropped, never written again (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The event's JSON file is version 2, a race's `durationMinutes` counted from its gun; a version 1 file reads and imports with the race's end it had (its minutes recounted from the gun when it has a gun and a start hour), and a version 1 race whose end was at or before its gun is refused as invalid naming `event.durationMinutes` (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: route checkpoints, cut-offs and the race's time limit (file v2)
